canonical_meanings: P027 initial frozen contract; supersedes historical unimplemented SEC placeholders

rules.description: Credible embedded credentials, tokens, API keys or private-key material in source/configuration.
false_negative_risks: Indirect, encrypted or externally assembled secrets may be missed.
false_positive_risks: Examples, placeholders and test fixtures may resemble credentials.
limitations: Arbitrary literals are not secret evidence; no secret entropy or validity detector yet.
rules.name: Hardcoded Secret
rules.remediation: Remove embedded secret material and use an appropriate secret-management boundary.

rules.description: Untrusted data reaches SQL construction/execution without recognized safe parameterization.
false_negative_risks: Framework wrappers and interprocedural flows require additional modeling.
false_positive_risks: Query text with safe bound parameters can resemble unsafe construction.
limitations: SQL text alone is insufficient; source/sink and parameterization semantics are required.
rules.name: SQL Injection Risk
rules.remediation: Use parameterized queries and verify the actual driver/framework boundary.

rules.description: Untrusted data reaches process/shell execution without an adequate safety boundary.
false_negative_risks: Indirect process APIs, wrappers and platform-specific shells may be missed.
false_positive_risks: Constant commands and appropriately restricted argument lists can look suspicious.
limitations: Constant process execution alone is insufficient; shell/argument semantics matter.
rules.name: Command Injection Risk
rules.remediation: Restrict executable and arguments and avoid unnecessary shell interpretation.

rules.description: Untrusted path/file input reaches filesystem operations without normalization/confinement.
false_negative_risks: Symlinks, encoded paths and cross-function validation need additional analysis.
false_positive_risks: Trusted paths and checked confinement boundaries can resemble unsafe access.
limitations: A file call alone is insufficient; normalization is not by itself proof of confinement.
rules.name: Path Traversal Risk
rules.remediation: Validate, normalize and confine paths to the intended authorized location.

rules.description: Known unsafe object deserialization or security-relevant deserialization of untrusted data.
false_negative_risks: Custom serializers and framework-specific object instantiation may be missed.
false_positive_risks: Constrained formats and trusted inputs can be mistaken for unsafe deserialization.
limitations: Ordinary JSON parsing is not automatically unsafe object deserialization.
rules.name: Unsafe Deserialization
rules.remediation: Use constrained formats and review trust, object types and deserialization settings.

rules.description: Attacker-controlled URL/host reaches server-side outbound network sinks without restriction.
false_negative_risks: Redirects, DNS resolution and indirect client wrappers require extra modeling.
false_positive_risks: Constant or adequately allowlisted requests can resemble SSRF sinks.
limitations: Constant outbound HTTP is insufficient; URL/host control and effective restrictions matter.
rules.name: Server-Side Request Forgery Risk
rules.remediation: Restrict outbound destinations and verify redirects, resolution and trust boundaries.

rules.description: Untrusted content reaches HTML/DOM rendering without adequate escaping/sanitization.
false_negative_risks: Dynamic rendering, template composition and framework behavior may be missed.
false_positive_risks: Automatically escaped templates and context-aware sanitizers can appear unsafe.
limitations: Generic output is insufficient; escaping is framework and rendering-context specific.
rules.name: Cross-Site Scripting Risk
rules.remediation: Use context-appropriate escaping/sanitization and review the actual rendering sink.

rules.description: Explicitly weak or security-inappropriate cryptographic primitives in sensitive contexts.
false_negative_risks: Indirect primitive selection and configuration-dependent behavior may be missed.
false_positive_risks: Non-security checksums and compatibility-only uses may resemble weak cryptography.
limitations: Ordinary non-security checksums are not automatically security findings.
rules.name: Weak Cryptography
rules.remediation: Select appropriate cryptographic primitives and review security-sensitive configuration.

rules.description: Non-cryptographic randomness is used for security-sensitive tokens, secrets or nonces.
false_negative_risks: Indirect token construction or custom randomness providers may be missed.
false_positive_risks: Non-security randomization may appear sensitive without usage context.
limitations: Ordinary simulation or UI randomness is insufficient evidence of security risk.
rules.name: Insecure Randomness
rules.remediation: Use cryptographically secure randomness for security-sensitive values.

rules.description: Attacker-controlled or insufficiently constrained data reaches dynamic code evaluation.
false_negative_risks: Custom evaluators, generated expressions and interprocedural constraints may be missed.
false_positive_risks: Constant expressions or effectively constrained evaluation may resemble unsafe execution.
limitations: Constant and tightly constrained evaluation require distinct contextual treatment.
rules.name: Unsafe Dynamic Code Execution
rules.remediation: Avoid unnecessary dynamic evaluation and strictly constrain permitted inputs and behavior.
